text_blocks.snippet: The Great Depression, which began in 1929 and lasted into the late 1930s, had profound and devastating effects on the United States and the world. Economically, it led to a dramatic decline in industrial production, soaring unemployment, and widespread bank failures. Socially, it resulted in poverty, homelessness, and increased reliance on government assistance. Politically, it spurred a re-evaluation of the role of government in the economy and led to the rise of interventionist policies.
